concerns: Status transitions are represented using raw Strings like 'PENDING' and 'RESOLVED' instead of type-safe Java Enums, making status handling more error-prone.
There is no length validation on commentText or requestText inputs, which could lead to large payloads causing out-of-memory errors or database storage overhead.
In addFavorite, if the favorite already exists, it silently returns an empty 200 OK without notifying the client that the record was already present.
The saved query text field length is constrained to 1000 in the database schema, but there is no length validation performed on the Java controller side prior to persisting.

PDF generation relies on hardcoded paths to system fonts ('/usr/share/fonts/truetype/...'). If these fonts are missing in the runtime environment, it falls back to Helvetica, which might cause Cyrillic characters to render as question marks.

Manual construction of the DOCX ZIP archive by concatenating raw XML string templates is highly fragile and prone to schema validation errors or corruption if special XML characters are not fully escaped.

Performing Levenshtein distance calculations in memory for every search query against all documents in the database does not scale and will lead to severe performance degradation as the database size increases.
Post-filtering and sorting scored documents in-memory scales poorly with larger collections; the database should ideally perform native full-text search with indexing.

verdicts.criticalReason: PR #5 contains a severe security vulnerability. During authentication (POST /api/v1/auth/login), the controller permits clients to specify their own 'role' in the JSON request body (defaulting to 'ADMINISTRATOR' if absent). If a user does not exist in the database, the system registers them dynamically and grants them the user-specified role, allowing unauthenticated clients to gain administrative rights. Additionally, resolveUser(String authHeader) updates a user's role in the database to match any role claim present in the parsed JWT, enabling privilege escalation.
concerns: Storing raw BCrypt-encoded passwords on first login for pre-existing users without checking their identity or verifying current authority is highly insecure.

The application-wide authorization mechanism depends entirely on resolveUser checking a bearer token without integrating into a proper security filter chain, leaving unannotated endpoints potentially unprotected.
